title: Afterlife researchers claim your 'mind could live on after death' - US News - News
excerpt: A Finland-based researcher has suggested that consciousness may persist after death, based on accounts of cardiac arrest survivors
content:
Near death experiences offer what many believe to be a glimpse into an afterlife (Image: Getty Images)

Groundbreaking research suggests consciousness could live on even after death.

Finland-based researcher Pekka Rechardt built the theory on testimonies from cardiac arrest survivors who described vivid experiences during periods of undetectable electrical brain activity.

The scientist looked at a 2025 review of near-death research by a team of international researchers who found that electrical activity in the outer layer of the brain can vanish within 10 to 30 seconds of cardiac arrest. The authors of that earlier review argued that some near-death experiences take place during this diminished period of brain activity.

Rechardt took those testimonies to show that consciousness does not rely entirely on brain activity. He said that these near-death experiences involved three fundamental components of awareness: a sense of being present, vivid sensations, and the capacity to experience events as a coherent whole.

He argues that if these three things can continue without the brain activity typically associated with consciousness, the destruction of the brain might not mean the end of the mind either.

"This empirical consideration supports life after death being a credible option," he wrote.

Using the scenario of someone walking along a beautiful beach, he argues that the experience engages distinct areas of the brain with neural signals requiring time to move around the brain.
